name: Atlassian MCP Server
use_label: Connect Jira and Confluence to AI tools
one_liner: Atlassian's official bridge that lets AI tools read and act on Jira, Confluence and the rest of the platform.

text.why: The work lives in Jira and Confluence, but AI tools cannot see inside them. This server bridges the two, so a request like "summarise what's left in this sprint" is answered from the real data. It is built and hosted by Atlassian itself.
text.take: Unofficial connectors existed before; what changes here is an official path where access and security are the vendor's responsibility — which matters when the data is your company's work.
build: Apache-2.0, cloud-hosted by Atlassian, covering Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Bitbucket, Compass, Loom and wider platform data through the Teamwork Graph.

who.role: Teams on Jira or Confluence who want AI tools in the loop, and managers who have been copying ticket status by hand.

start.text: Open the getting-started guide at atlassian.com/platform/rovo-mcp to connect it to your AI tool, and check first whether your admin has to approve it.

caveat: Atlassian Cloud only. Company accounts may need admin approval, and since the connected AI tool can read work data, check the permission scope first.

license.scope_text: Commercial use, redistribution OK. Keep notices; mark changes.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: The Atlassian MCP Server page explaining how AI tools connect to Jira and Confluence.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.
